mood.summary: GIFT Nifty was at 22,677.5 (−70.5) at 6:54 AM, about 130 points below Wednesday's Nifty close of 22,811, so a soft start is likely. Wall Street rose (Nasdaq +1.05%), Asia is mixed early Thursday (Nikkei +0.22%, Kospi flat) and Meta gained about 3% after hours, but Brent is back above $110 after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and a US order for some diplomats to leave the kingdom. At home, the RBI's minutes say rate cuts are off the table and CPI may touch 6% this quarter, India VIX is at a four-month high, and smallcaps fell 2.37% on Wednesday with only 608 shares rising against 2,988 falling. Support comes from a rupee at a six-week high (94.38), IT strength and strong Eternal results; Nifty's support is 22,650 (Wednesday's low), then 22,500–22,400, with 23,000 and 23,175 as hurdles.

news.headline: GIFT Nifty at 22,677 points to a soft open
news.summary: GIFT Nifty was down 70.5 points (0.31%) at 22,677.5, around 130 points below Nifty's Wednesday close and below the October futures price of 22,745.
news.why: Puts Nifty near Wednesday's 22,650 low at the open; a break there brings 22,500–22,400 into view.

news.headline: Nifty slips 0.34% to 22,811; smallcaps fall 2.37% as VIX hits 4-month high
news.summary: Nifty gave up an early rise to 23,120 and closed at 22,811.35, Sensex at 73,709.69 and Bank Nifty at 54,976.90 (−0.92%). Only 608 NSE shares rose against 2,988 that fell; India VIX jumped up to 9.5% intraday.
news.why: Very weak breadth and rising volatility show broad selling under the surface; IT alone held the index up.

news.headline: US orders some diplomats out of Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks; Brent tops $110
news.summary: Iran-aligned Houthis struck targets in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, including a drone attack on an oil field that killed two and a strike on Dammam airport. The US told some diplomats and families to leave; Brent rose 1.2% to $110.11.
news.why: Higher oil feeds inflation and weakens the rupee; it hurts oil marketers, paints, airlines and chemicals, and helps upstream producers.

news.headline: RBI minutes: rate cuts off the table; CPI may touch 6% this quarter
news.summary: Minutes of the 5–7 Oct meeting show all six members backed the 25 bps hike to 5.50%. Governor Malhotra said the next move is a hike or a pause; CPI is forecast at 6.0% in Oct–Dec, while the FY27 GDP forecast was raised to 7.1%. Two members preferred a neutral stance.
news.why: Raises the odds of another hike on 4 Dec, a negative for NBFCs, housing finance, realty and autos.

news.headline: Wall Street rises on AI optimism; Meta up 3% after hours, Tesla down 2%
news.summary: Dow +0.69%, S&P 500 +0.58% and Nasdaq +1.05% as SpaceX and Super Micro results lifted chip stocks. Meta beat on revenue ($64.6 bn) and guided Q4 to $73–76 bn; Tesla beat on earnings but slipped after hours.
news.why: Supports Indian IT stocks; the late fade on Gulf news limits the read-through.

news.headline: Asia mixed early Thursday: Nikkei edges up, Kospi trims losses before Bank of Korea decision
news.summary: Nikkei 225 opened slightly lower but turned 0.22% higher at 64,764.54; Kospi opened 1.1% down after Wednesday's 3.3% rally and later traded flat at 5,732.23. The Bank of Korea decides rates today with the base rate at 3%.
news.why: No strong lead from Asia, so Indian trade will be set mainly by oil, the Gulf news and Q2 results.

news.headline: Rupee closes at six-week high of 94.38 on Jio IPO inflows
news.summary: The rupee gained 53 paise to 94.38 per dollar, its best close since early September, helped by foreign inflows for the Jio Platforms IPO and RBI action. A range of 94.20–94.80 is expected.
news.why: A firmer rupee eases imported inflation and FII currency losses, but trims gold ETF and IT export gains.

news.headline: FIIs sell ₹1,022 cr, DIIs buy ₹1,614 cr on Wednesday
news.summary: Provisional data show FIIs as net sellers for a second session and DIIs as buyers. PTI reported the same FII amount as a purchase, so the direction should be checked on the NSE site.
news.why: Steady FII selling keeps pressure on large banks and financials; DII buying limits the fall.

news.headline: Jio Platforms IPO subscribed 3.16 times on day 1; retail portion 0.73x
news.summary: The ₹30,213 cr issue drew 9.42x from institutions and 1.68x from HNIs on the first day, but retail demand was below 1x. The issue closes on 23 Oct.
news.why: Strong demand supports Reliance's valuation; the issue may also tie up some market money until allotment on 26 Oct.

news.headline: Q2 results today: HPCL, Havells, Swiggy, Colgate, Cyient, CreditAccess and about 18 more
news.summary: About 24 companies report on Thursday, including HPCL, Chennai Petroleum, Adani Total Gas, Adani Energy Solutions, Colgate-Palmolive, Hatsun Agro, Havells, Cyient, Nuvoco, CreditAccess Grameen, Swiggy and Bluestone.
news.why: Oil marketers report with Brent above $110, so HPCL's marketing margin comments matter for HPCL, BPCL and IOC; Swiggy will be compared with Eternal's strong numbers.

news.headline: Eternal Q2 profit jumps 92% to ₹125 cr; revenue up 78%
news.summary: Revenue rose to ₹24,138 cr and EBITDA to ₹752 cr (margin 3.1%). Blinkit's order value rose 79% to ₹20,940 cr with 308 new stores, and its adjusted EBITDA rose to ₹184 cr.
news.why: Quick commerce turning more profitable is the key test for the stock, which fell 2.7% before the results.

news.headline: IT index hits 8-month high; LTTS jumps 10.7% on results
news.summary: Nifty IT rose 2.88% with every stock up. LTTS gained 10.66% after large deal wins (AI-led deals over half the total); Infosys rose 3.3% on an expanded Truist deal ahead of results on 23 Oct.
news.why: IT is the market's main support while oil and rate worries hit other sectors.

news.headline: HDFC Bank opens internal probe into alleged information leak by two senior executives
news.summary: The bank confirmed an internal review after reports that two senior executives leaked confidential information; it gave no details. The probe comes days before Anup Bagchi takes over as CEO (Jagdishan's term ends 26 Oct).
news.why: Governance headlines can weigh on the heaviest Nifty bank stock during the leadership change.

news.headline: Adani Green Q2 profit up 16% to ₹747 cr, but shares fall about 4%
news.summary: Revenue rose 42% to ₹4,258 cr and EBITDA 46% to ₹3,797 cr; energy sales grew 33% and capacity reached 20.8 GW. The stock fell to ₹1,247.95 intraday.
news.why: Profit grew far slower than revenue because of higher costs; the market wanted more.

news.headline: IHCL Q2 profit up 22.6%; FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 15–17%
news.summary: Indian Hotels' profit rose to ₹350 cr on 21.7% revenue growth. Management raised its full-year revenue growth guidance and is targeting 700 hotels.
news.why: Raised guidance in a weak market is a positive signal for hotel stocks.

news.headline: M&M Finance Q2 profit up 55% to ₹882 cr as credit costs fall
news.summary: Loan growth and lower credit costs drove the jump; NDTV Profit reports the consolidated figure as ₹909 cr (+61%), with NII up 12.5%.
news.why: Better asset quality in rural vehicle finance after a strong festive season.

news.headline: Persistent Systems launches QIP of up to $450 mn; floor price ₹5,761
news.summary: The IT company opened a qualified institutional placement with a revised floor of ₹5,761 a share and a possible discount of up to 5%. Crisil rates it AA+.
news.why: New shares dilute holders and the discount can pull the price toward the floor for a few days.

news.headline: BEL wins orders worth ₹1,011 cr since 13 Oct
news.summary: Bharat Electronics said it secured orders worth ₹1,011 cr since its last disclosure on 13 Oct; clients and execution periods were not detailed in the source.
news.why: Adds to a large order book; small relative to BEL's size, so the price effect is usually modest.

gold.label: Down ~0.6% Wed
gold.summary: MCX December gold fell 0.57% to ₹1,45,678 per 10g on Wednesday while spot gold held near $4,128–4,150, so the fall came mainly from the rupee's jump to a six-week high (94.38). Gold ETFs like GOLDBEES may stay soft at the open, though the fresh Gulf attacks give some safe-haven support. Expect ₹1,44,000–1,47,665 until the 28 Oct Fed decision.
gold.how: Indian gold ETFs track the domestic gold rate: world gold in dollars × USD/INR, plus import duty. So both world events and the rupee move them.

scenarios.title: Dollar slides again
scenarios.why: The dollar index rose to 102 and the US 10-year yield to 5.14% on Monday, which pushed gold below $4,150. A renewed slide would lift world gold; a firmer rupee would trim part of the gain for Indian ETFs.
scenarios.line: Dollar flat at 101.7; gold needs a softer dollar to regain $4,185.

scenarios.title: Fed holds on 28 Oct (~88% odds)
scenarios.why: Prediction markets price about 88% odds of no change. A clear pause keeps yields and the dollar steady, helping gold toward $4,185–4,239; a firmer rupee would trim part of the gain in India.
scenarios.line: A hold is priced; gold needs soft guidance to clear $4,185.

scenarios.title: Fed hikes on 28 Oct (~11% odds)
scenarios.why: Hike odds have fallen since the hot September CPI and PPI, but a surprise move would lift the dollar and yields and could push gold back toward $4,000–4,066. FII selling in India would likely rise, weakening the rupee and cushioning part of the fall.
scenarios.line: Hike odds have fallen; gold toward $4,050–4,100 if it happens.

scenarios.title: Gulf conflict widens, oil spikes
scenarios.why: Gold usually jumps on war fears, and higher oil weakens the rupee, so Indian gold ETFs gain on both counts. The catch: costly oil also feeds inflation and Fed-hike fears, which has capped gold's rallies recently, so gains can fade.
scenarios.when: 21 Oct: Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, US orders diplomats out; Brent $110.11 on 22 Oct
scenarios.line: Saudi attacks lifted Brent to $110; war would lift gold and weaken the rupee.

scenarios.title: US–Iran de-escalation
scenarios.why: Less war risk removes some safe-haven buying, though cheaper oil also lowers inflation and hike fears, which helps gold. The clearer effect for India is a stronger rupee, which pulls the rupee price of gold down.
scenarios.when: FT: Israeli strike shelved by Trump; Iran's president says talks impossible under blockade
scenarios.line: Less haven demand and a stronger rupee pull Indian gold down.

scenarios.title: Rupee slides past 97
scenarios.why: Every 1% fall in the rupee adds roughly 1% to Indian gold ETF prices even if world gold is flat. FII selling and Brent above $110 are the pressures, but Jio IPO inflows and RBI action have strengthened the rupee.
scenarios.line: Each 1% rupee fall adds ~1% to gold ETFs, even with gold flat.

scenarios.title: Rupee recovers
scenarios.why: Jio IPO inflows and RBI action lifted the rupee to a six-week high on Wednesday, which is why MCX gold fell while world gold was flat. Further gains would keep pressure on Indian gold ETFs.
scenarios.when: Rupee at six-week high 94.38 on 21 Oct; range seen 94.20–94.80
scenarios.line: Rupee rose 53 paise Wed; each 1% gain cuts ~1% off gold ETFs.

scenarios.title: Stock market sell-off
scenarios.why: Investors move money into gold when stocks fall. The WGC says weak Indian equities drove gold ETF buying in September. In a severe crash gold can dip briefly as people sell everything to raise cash, then recover.
scenarios.when: Smallcap 100 −2.37% and VIX at 4-month high on 21 Oct
scenarios.line: Broad sell-off Wed (608 up vs 2,988 down); deeper falls push money to gold.

scenarios.title: Central banks keep buying
scenarios.why: China's central bank added 21 tonnes in September, its 23rd straight monthly purchase. Steady official buying tends to limit how far gold falls, though it rarely drives short-term moves.
scenarios.line: China added 21 t in Sept (23rd month); limits downside.

scenarios.title: India cuts import duty
scenarios.why: Indian gold ETFs track the domestic price, which includes customs duty. A duty cut would lower the Indian gold price, and ETF prices, overnight by about the size of the cut, as happened in the July 2024 Budget. A duty hike would do the opposite.
scenarios.line: Domestic gold, and ETFs, drop overnight by about the cut.

guide._all: Each card is a company-specific event from the latest filings and news. Green = likely to support the share, red = likely to pressure it, amber = watch. Wednesday-evening results (Eternal, IHCL, M&M Finance, KEI, PC Jeweller) get their first reaction today. No client-loss or order-cancellation news found since the last update. Review-by dates are counted in trading days (10 Nov is a market holiday).
guide.Can rise: Positive triggers. A share does not always rise on good news, especially if it ran up before the announcement or the overall market is weak.
guide.Can fall: Negative triggers. Results misses, big investor exits and weak business updates usually hit the share on the day and can weigh for weeks.
guide.Order won: An order matters most when it is big compared with the company's yearly revenue (5–10% or more is significant for smaller companies). Repeat orders and orders in a new area are good signs of future growth. Check the execution period: a 24-month order adds revenue slowly. Being named the only qualified bidder (Goodluck) is a step before an order, not an order itself.
guide.Results: Shares react to results versus expectations, not just growth. Profit growing slower than sales signals squeezed margins, in-line results after a run-up often get sold (Nestle), and guidance for the next quarter can matter more than the quarter itself (Wipro). The earnings call commentary often matters as much as the numbers.
guide.Business update: Monthly sales, pre-sales and festive data give an early read on the quarter before results come out.
guide.Board decision: Board outcomes that usually lift a share: buyback, bonus, stock split, special dividend, demerger or merger that simplifies the group. Ones that can pressure it: big equity fund raise (QIP or rights issue) that adds new shares, large acquisitions that need fresh capital (Aegis), or large related-party deals.
guide.Stake sale: When a promoter or big investor sells in a block deal, the share often falls on the day because the sale is at a discount. If quality institutions buy, it usually recovers within weeks.
guide.Regulatory: For pharma: a USFDA warning letter or import alert is a big negative, while a Form 483 with a few procedural observations (Dr Reddy's) is usually minor. Approvals, certifications and cuts in tax demands (Paytm) are positives; new or higher tax demands (Mphasis) and lawsuits (Bank of Baroda) are negatives, though most are disputed for years. Rule changes by NPCI, SEBI or the exchanges (UPI fees, F&O exits) can move a whole group of stocks.
guide.Management change: A sudden exit of a CEO or CFO can spook investors; a planned succession usually doesn't.
guide.Corporate action: Takeovers, open offers and delisting plans. These change who owns the company and can create short-term price moves. If the share already trades above the deal price (IDBI Bank), the upside depends on the open-offer terms.
guide.Fund raise: Debt or government loans don't dilute shareholders. Equity raises (QIP, rights, preferential issue) add new shares and can weigh on the price.
guide.Legal claim: A lawsuit or legal claim against a company. A big headline number can hit the share for days, but most claims take years and are often dismissed or settled for far less. Watch whether the court admits the case and what the company files.

items.title: India–US trade deal
items.who: Commerce Ministry and US Trade Representative
items.latest: 21 Oct: Rubio said the deal is 'incredibly close' and should come 'in a matter of weeks, not months', with only technical drafting left; he toured Reliance's Jamnagar refinery and pushed for more US energy purchases. Goyal says the pact is done but India wants a tariff edge over Vietnam, Bangladesh and Thailand; Sitharaman says talks have plateaued. The US rate on most Indian goods is 18% under the February framework. Goyal visits Germany and the Netherlands 22–27 Oct.
items.effect: A deal that lowers US tariffs would help exporters that depend on the US: textiles and apparel, gems and jewellery, auto parts, chemicals, seafood. Failure or new tariffs would hit the same group.
items.when: Announcement 'within weeks' per Rubio; leaders' signing could follow
items.likely: Medium to high: both sides say it is close, but nothing signed
items.watch: Any announcement during Rubio's visit; tariff rates for textiles, gems, auto parts, chemicals

items.title: RBI rate decision: another hike likely in December
items.latest: 21 Oct: Minutes of the 5–7 Oct meeting show all six members voted for the 25 bps hike to 5.50%; Governor Malhotra said rate cuts are off the table and the next move is a hike or pause. CPI is forecast at 6.0% in Oct–Dec and 5.7% in Jan–Mar; FY27 GDP forecast raised to 7.1%. Two members (Nagesh Kumar, Ram Singh) preferred a neutral stance.
items.effect: A hike raises borrowing costs: negative for rate-sensitive stocks such as NBFCs, real estate and autos, and for bond prices. Banks can gain on margins at first. A pause would be a relief rally trigger.
items.likely: High for another 25 bps hike if October CPI stays near 6%
items.watch: October CPI (12 Nov), liquidity operations, rupee and crude

items.title: US midterm elections and Iran risk
items.latest: 21 Oct: The FT reported Israel had prepared a large multi-day strike on Iran for mid-October that was shelved after Trump opposed renewed war before the 3 Nov midterms. Same day, Houthi drones killed two at a Saudi oil field, the US ordered some diplomats out of Saudi Arabia, and Iran's IRGC said Hormuz is 'completely closed'. Brent was $110.11 early Thursday.
items.effect: After 3 Nov the Iran pledge expires, so oil and safe-haven risk could rise. Higher oil hurts India (rupee, inflation, oil marketing companies, paints, airlines) and helps gold and upstream oil.
items.watch: Post-3 Nov Iran decisions, Israel's 27 Oct election, Gulf shipping attacks, Brent above $110

items.title: US Federal Reserve rate decision
items.latest: Fed is in its pre-meeting blackout. Kalshi prices about 88% odds of a hold on 27–28 Oct and 11% for a hike. The US 10-year yield was 5.13% on 21 Oct (+1 bp).
items.effect: A hold is mildly positive for Indian stocks, the rupee and gold. A surprise hike would lift the dollar and US yields, push FIIs to sell more, and hurt IT and gold.
items.watch: No major US data this week; the 28 Oct statement and any December hike hints

items.title: US waives sanctions on Russian energy exports
items.latest: Around 18 Oct Trump waived Graham Act sanctions and tariffs on Russian energy exports. On 21 Oct the Kremlin said Putin agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month, and a US official said Russia accepted a trilateral meeting.
items.effect: More Russian oil on the market eases crude prices and lowers the risk of US penalties on Indian refiners that buy Russian crude: positive for oil marketing companies, airlines, paints and the rupee.
items.likely: Done; Congress critics could push back
items.watch: Whether the waiver lasts and Brent's reaction to Hormuz news

items.title: OPEC+ oil output for December
items.latest: On 4–5 Oct OPEC+ kept November output unchanged. The next monthly decision (for December) is due in early November.
items.effect: Higher output would ease crude and help India's rupee, inflation and oil marketing companies. A cut would do the opposite.
items.watch: Brent ~$108 (19 Oct) after the US Russia-sanctions waiver

items.title: IDBI Bank sold to Fairfax (60.72% stake at ₹81/share)
items.latest: On 14 Oct the Cabinet approved Fairfax's ₹52,878 cr bid: the government sells 30.48% and LIC 30.24% at ₹81 a share. IDBI jumped 9% to ₹90.39 on 14 Oct, then fell 8.1% to ₹83.07 on 15 Oct. Fairfax reportedly plans to combine IDBI Bank, Digit Insurance and IIFL Capital into one group. On 16 Oct Business Standard reported Fairfax proposes contributing Digit Insurance and IIFL Capital to IDBI Bank; CSB Bank denied merger talks with IDBI. On 17–19 Oct IDBI reported Q2 profit down 39% to ₹2,205 cr (the year-ago figure had a one-off ₹1,699 cr NSDL gain).
items.effect: Largest privatisation since Air India and a boost to reform sentiment. For IDBI shareholders, the stock already trades above ₹81; open-offer terms for public shareholders are not yet announced, so chasing the jump is risky. Fairfax must merge or exit CSB Bank, where it owns 40%.
items.likely: High (approved); RBI fit-and-proper and CCI clearances still needed
items.watch: Open-offer price and size; RBI approval; government's plan to sell its remaining 15%

items.title: Scrap LTCG tax on shares (and possibly cut STT)
items.who: Proposed by SBI Research · Decision: Finance Ministry
items.latest: SBI Research (12 Oct) proposed scrapping long-term capital gains tax on equities, with a 2–3 year holding period, to stem FPI outflows of ₹3.04 lakh cr this year. On 14 Oct the Finance Minister said it is 'too early to comment' and announced no change. On 19 Oct, Bernstein said an LTCG cut alone won't bring back FPIs and cut its Nifty target to 25,000.
items.effect: If done, a big positive for the whole market and for FPI flows; brokers, exchanges and AMCs would gain most. Current LTCG is 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh. A cut in STT on F&O (raised to 0.05% on futures in April) would mainly help brokers and BSE.
items.likely: Low to medium: equity LTCG brought in about ₹1.29 lakh cr, hard to give up with a ~4.5% fiscal deficit
items.watch: Pre-Budget consultations (Nov–Jan) and any Finance Ministry comment

items.title: SEBI closing auction for the final price
items.latest: SEBI finalised the rules on 15 Oct: a 10-minute closing auction from 3:30 to 3:40 PM on all trading days, index and stock derivatives trading until 3:45 PM (some expiring index contracts excepted), and expiring derivatives settled on the volume-weighted average price of the last 30 minutes.
items.effect: Changes how the closing price is set. Mainly affects traders, index funds and exchanges; little effect on long-term holders. BSE was among today's top Nifty losers (−1.8%).
items.when: Most changes from 7 Dec 2026; limit/iceberg orders into the auction from 8 Feb 2027
items.watch: Exchange circulars and broker system changes

items.title: 0.4% UPI merchant fee on payments above ₹2,000
items.latest: On 13 Oct NPCI deferred the 0.4% merchant discount rate on certain UPI merchant payments above ₹2,000 until after Diwali; a new date will be notified.
items.effect: A fee on large UPI merchant payments would give payment companies a revenue source; small merchants would bear the cost. Positive for payment firms such as Paytm when it starts.
items.when: After Diwali (8 Nov); new date to be notified
items.watch: NPCI circular with the start date

items.title: More PSU stake sales (OFS) this year
items.latest: About ₹55,757 cr raised so far in FY27 from stake sales in 9 PSUs (including LIC and Coal India). With IDBI, receipts cross the ₹80,000 cr target for the first time in 8 years. The government may sell its residual IDBI stake in the market.
items.effect: An offer-for-sale (OFS) is usually priced at a discount, so the PSU stock often dips for a few days around the sale. Meeting the target can reduce pressure for further big sales this year.
items.when: Through March 2027; OFS dates are announced a day ahead
items.watch: OFS announcements on NSE/BSE (usually the evening before)

items.title: Union Budget 2027
items.latest: Preparations are under way. The LTCG/STT debate, disinvestment, capex and the fiscal deficit (~4.5% of GDP) will be the key themes.
items.effect: Tax changes on capital gains or STT, customs duty on gold, and capex plans can move whole sectors on the day.
items.watch: Pre-Budget meetings and leaks from December
